advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits a classic God Object pattern, evidenced by a high Number of Methods (NOM=25) and a Critical Lack of Cohesion (LCOM4=4). The code is explicitly partitioned into four distinct functional components (Order Management, Pricing, Audit Logging, and Notification) that share no attributes, indicating that the class is a container for unrelated responsibilities rather than a cohesive unit. While the Data Attribute Metric (DAM=1.0) suggests good encapsulation, the high coupling to 8 distinct classes (DCC=8) and the high Weighted Methods per Class (WMC=49) confirm that the class is overly complex and difficult to maintain or test in isolation.

suggestions.title: Extract Pricing and Shipping Logic
suggestions.sketch: Create a new class `PricingService` (or `PricingEngine`) that encapsulates `self._tax_rate` and `self._discount_rules`. Move the methods `set_discount`, `discount_for`, `bulk_discount`, `set_tax_rate`, `apply_tax`, `total_with_tax`, and `shipping_for` into this new class. `OrderManager` should hold an instance of `PricingService` and delegate pricing calculations to it. This removes the pricing component from the LCOM4 graph, significantly reducing the cohesion score and method count of `OrderManager`.

suggestions.title: Extract Audit Logging Functionality
suggestions.sketch: Create a new class `AuditLogger` that encapsulates `self._log`. Move the methods `log_event`, `history`, `last_event`, `log_size`, and `clear_log` into this class. `OrderManager` should hold an instance of `AuditLogger` and call its methods when order state changes occur (e.g., in `place_order` or `cancel_order`). This isolates the logging concern, further reducing the LCOM4 and NOM of the main class.

suggestions.title: Extract Notification Handling
suggestions.sketch: Create a new class `NotificationService` that encapsulates `self._smtp_host` and `self._sent`. Move the methods `configure_smtp`, `notify`, `sent_count`, `outbox`, and `reset_outbox` into this class. `OrderManager` should hold an instance of `NotificationService` and delegate email sending tasks to it. This removes the notification component from the LCOM4 graph, addressing the final major source of incohesion.

advices.risk_notes: Refactoring will increase the number of classes in the project, potentially raising the overall system complexity if not managed well. The DCC (Data Coupling) of the new `OrderManager` will increase as it must now reference the new service classes. Additionally, any existing code that directly accesses `OrderManager`'s pricing, logging, or notification methods will need to be updated to use the new service interfaces. Testing will need to be updated to mock or instantiate these new services.
